newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian court adjourns Rao hearing until Oct 30.
newsitem.headline: Indian court adjourns Rao hearing until Oct 30.

text.p: An Indian court on Monday adjourned a hearing on a request by former prime minister P.V. Narasimha Rao for an extension of temporary bail in a forgery case until October 30, United News of India (UNI).
Last month, federal police charged Rao and five others with using false documents in 1989 to try to defame a rival politician.
Last week, Rao was briefly arrested on forgery and related charges at his home in the Indian capital, then immediately released on temporary bail.
A Delhi court was scheduled on Monday to take up a request by Rao to have the temporary bail extended until the completion of the trial in the case.
UNI said the court quickly adjourned Monday's hearing and rescheduled it for October 30. UNI did not indicate whether Rao's temporary bail was extended until that date.
Rao has been summoned to appear in court on Wednesday in a separate case of criminal conspiracy to cheat.
However, it was not clear whether that hearing would be held as the Supreme Court has ordered any court appearances by Rao to be held away from the local courts in a more secure location.
The substitute location has not yet been selected.
